title: 7 Costly Mistakes After a Crash in New York
metaDescription: 7 costly mistakes after a New York crash: recorded statements, gaps in care, and missing the 3-yr SOL.
excerpt: Educational New York, NY guide — 3-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: Mistake 1: Skipping medical care
paragraphs: Delayed treatment is the top reason New York adjusters reduce offers. Visit NYU Langone within 24 hours when pain exists.

sections.heading: Mistake 2: Recorded statements
paragraphs: Adjusters are trained to elicit admissions. Politely decline until you understand injuries and coverage.

sections.heading: Mistake 3: Social media
paragraphs: Posts, check-ins, and photos can contradict injury claims — even innocent updates.

sections.heading: Mistake 4: Missing the 3-year deadline
paragraphs: New York courts enforce statutes strictly. Calendar your deadline the day you are injured.

sections.heading: Mistake 5: Accepting the first check
paragraphs: Initial offers rarely include future medical care or wage loss on FDR Drive / West Side Highway crashes.

sections.heading: Mistake 6: Poor crash report follow-up
paragraphs: Obtain the official report and verify accuracy — errors on New York County (Manhattan) reports are correctable in some cases.

sections.heading: Mistake 7: DIY negotiation on serious injuries
paragraphs: Complex New York crashes involving surgery, permanent impairment, or commercial vehicles usually need professional evaluation.

faq.question: Is this legal advice for my New York case?
faq.answer: No. This is general education from WreckMatch LLC, a referral service — not a law firm. Consult a licensed attorney for advice about your situation.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in New York?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 3-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.
